case_name: Brijendra Singh vs State Of M.P. & Anr
facts_of_case: Mishri Bai, a crippled lady, was given in marriage to Padam Singh. She claims to have adopted Brijendra Singh. The Sub-Divisional Officer served a notice on Mishri Bai under the M.P. Ceiling on Agricultural Holdings Act, 1960.

legal_principles.principle: A Hindu wife cannot adopt a son or daughter to herself even with the consent of her husband.
legal_principles.held: It follows from Clause (c) of Section 8 that Hindu wife cannot adopt a son or daughter to herself even with the consent of her husband because the Section expressly provides for cases in which she can adopt a son or daughter to herself during the life time of the husband.
applicable_acts_sections: Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act, 1956 — Section 8

legal_principles.principle: A female Hindu has the capacity and right to have both adopted son and adopted daughter provided there is compliance of the requirements and conditions of such adoption laid down in the Act.
legal_principles.held: It follows from the language of Section 8 read with Clauses (i)& (ii) of Section 11 that the female Hindu has the capacity and right to have both adopted son and adopted daughter provided there is compliance of the requirements and conditions of such adoption laid down in the Act.
applicable_acts_sections: Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act, 1956 — Section 8
Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act, 1956 — Section 11
